correctness.rationale: For any face of the open-neighborhood complex a common neighbor forbids its own color, so the coloring gives a simplicial map to the tetrahedron boundary. For a one-site move the union of the two images still avoids the common neighbor's color if that neighbor is unchanged; if it is the recolored vertex, the face itself has no changed vertex. Hence the two maps are contiguous. The signed 20-triangle chain is closed and pushes forward to a multiple of the oriented tetrahedron boundary; a palette permutation acts on that boundary by its sign. A separate exact enumeration using the listed graph and chain found no three-coloring, 18,024 labeled four-colorings, 64,320 undirected one-vertex moves and exactly two 9,012-state components, with degrees +1 and −1 on the respective components. It also checked the signs under all 24 label permutations. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/021d8330-e34a-4dae-8fd5-a6e9399be218/independent_check.py. The bound scripts and logs were inspected but not executed.

value.rationale: At the chromatic threshold on a canonical triangle-free four-chromatic graph, identifying exactly how single-site connectivity differs from Kempe connectivity is a natural question. The open-neighborhood cycle gives a topological reason for a persistent obstruction under legal moves, not merely a bare coloring tally. That mathematical use is independent of whether the classification is distinctive in the corpus.
